title: The finale and beyond
game_role: The rooms, items and locked treasure door run on your play() function.
objective: Combine everything you learned in 30 days and write the final version of Piko's Adventure
story: You're at the summit of Python Mountain! Looking back from here, the road seems so long: you've come all the way from your first print to writing APIs. Piko is very proud. One last adventure remains: combining everything you've learned into a single game.

sections.title: What did you learn in 30 days?
sections.body:
- **Basics:** print, variables, operators, strings
- **Data structures:** list, tuple, set, dictionary
- **Flow:** conditions and loops
- **Tools:** functions, modules, list comprehensions, higher-order functions
- **Robustness:** error types, try/except, regular expressions, files
- **The world:** packages, virtual environments, classes, web scraping, statistics, pandas, the web, databases, APIs

That's a toolbox real programmers use every day!

sections.title: Good programmer habits
sections.body:
- **Move in small steps:** write a little, run it, then continue
- **Care about names:** `score` instead of `x`, `move_player` instead of `f`
- **Read the errors:** an error message is your best teacher
- **Turn repeated code into a function**
- **Ask when you're stuck:** a friend, a teacher, or the documentation

sections.title: What can you do next?
sections.body:
- **Games:** windowed, graphical games with `pygame`
- **Web:** publish your own site with `Flask`
- **Data:** tell data stories with `pandas` and charting packages
- **Automation:** let Python do repetitive computer chores
- **Artificial intelligence:** the basics of machine learning are learned with Python too

Keep the code you wrote in this book: each piece could be the start of a new adventure.

sections.title: The final adventure
sections.body:
In today's project task you'll write the heart of the game: a Piko who walks between rooms, collects items and opens the treasure door with a key. Dictionaries, loops, conditions and functions all together!

With this piece, all the parts you wrote over 30 days come together in a single game: your welcome screen, your hero's info, your score calculation, your move function, your battle rules...

When you finish the tasks, you've completed the 30-day adventure; the certificate at the end of the book is waiting for you. Congratulations, you're a Python programmer now!

tasks.title: Word counter
tasks.prompt: The `word_counts(text)` function should return a dictionary with how many times each word appears in the text.

tasks.title: Counter class
tasks.prompt: The `Counter` class should start at 0. `increment()` raises the counter by 1 and returns the new value, `reset()` sets it back to zero. The value is kept in the `value` attribute.
tasks.starter:
class Counter:
    pass

c = Counter()
c.increment()
print(c.increment())
hints: Inside increment: self.value += 1 and return self.value

challenge.title: Command engine
challenge.prompt:
Write a `run(commands)` function that changes a hero's state with a list of commands. Start: `{"hp": 10, "gold": 0}`.

- `"dig 5"`: gold goes up by 5
- `"fight 3"`: health goes down by 3
- `"potion"`: health goes up by 5 but can't go above 10
- Other commands are ignored. If health drops to 0 or below, the remaining commands don't run.

The function should return the final state as a dictionary.
hints: Check health after every command; if it's 0 or below, break

project_task.title: The final adventure
project_task.prompt:
The final version of Piko's Adventure! The `rooms` dictionary holds the rooms, their exits and the item in each room. The `play(commands)` function should start Piko in `"camp"` and apply the commands in order:

- `"go <direction>"`: if there's an exit in that direction, go there; otherwise print `You can't go there!`.
- `"take"`: if there's an item in the room, put it in the bag and remove it from the room.
- If Piko enters the `"treasure"` room **with the key**, print `Congratulations! You found the treasure.` and end the game. Without the key, print `The door is locked!` and stay put.

At the end the function should return `(current_room, sorted_bag_list)`.
hints: Check "key" in bag before entering the treasure room.
When the game ends, leave the loop with break.
